passages.provision_quote: For any employee who customarily and regularly receives tips or gratuities from patrons or others, the employer may pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute if the employer can establish by the employer's records of charged tips or gratuities or by the employee’s declaration for federal insurance contributions act purposes that for each week, when adding tips or gratuities received to wages paid, the employee received not less than the minimum wage plus $2 for all hours worked. Compliance with this section is determined by averaging tips or gratuities received by the employee over the course of the employer’s payroll period or any other period selected by the employer that complies with laws enacted by the legislature.
passages.note: Bill text amends the tipped-worker subminimum wage only; it states no general wage-floor rule.
Bill status page records the House Third Reading vote stage; sponsor listed is Mesnard, not Livingston.
House Third Reading roll call shows Livingston voted Y on SCR1040.

rows.reasoning: Livingston voted Y on SCR1040's House Third Reading (04/03/2024), a constitutional amendment letting employers pay tipped workers up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage. This is a tipped-wage subminimum change, not a statement of the general rule the ladder asks about ("Raise the wage floor...", "Hold the wage floor at its current level and let the market set pay above it"), so per the annex hard case on tipped-wage changes it shows direction only and establishes no rung.
needs_source: Livingston's own words or a record addressing the general minimum-wage floor, not limited to the tipped subminimum
